scope: Published supported-1.35 NPD source upgrade with all-three-program compiler and two-package APT patches. Not production acceptance, a fully patched Debian rootfs, exploitability assessment or forensic clearance.

go_advisories.scope: Actual source and all three symbolled published ELFs; raw records retained in the publication artifact, not general hostile-input or future-advisory clearance.

local_published_os_scan.scope: Exact published image OS-only local scan; not a natural cluster report. Counts are package/CVE tuples, not unique vulnerabilities or exploits. All severities including UNKNOWN retained.
remaining_assessment: Remaining HIGH/CRITICAL rows declare no fixed bookworm version in this actual Debian-backed report; do not downgrade to older security-index packages or infer unaffected status.
Debian qualifies CVE-2023-45853 because bookworm zlib does not build the affected MiniZip component; raw CRITICAL is retained, not waived or erased.
The systemd-homed record is component-specific, not evidence that every libsystemd call is vulnerable. This is not a blanket clearance.
CVE-2026-76844 has conflicting webpack description versus Debian zlib assignment. Retain the conflict and CVE-2026-85091 rather than silently discarding either.
CGO journal helpers use dlopen: direct DT_NEEDED libc-only output does not establish complete dynamic-library reachability.
Other local mount/partition, gzip, ACL, PAM namespace, infocmp and Perl ArchiveTar records remain unresolved; unused-command assumptions are not exploitability proof.
